messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The answer depends on whether you’re talking about planets in our own Solar System or about planets that have been found elsewhere in the galaxy.

| Context | Largest known planet |
|---------|----------------------|
| **Solar System** | **Jupiter** – about 11 times the radius of Earth and roughly 318 times its mass. |
| **Exoplanets (outside the Solar System)** | **HD 100546 b** – a “super‑Jupiter” with a radius ≈ 2.5 × Jupiter’s radius and a mass of about 10–15 Jupiter masses. It is currently the largest planet that has been confirmed by observations. |

> **Why HD 100546 b?**  
> HD 100546 b was discovered in 2013 around the young star HD 100546, located about 335 light‑years from Earth. Its size and mass place it at the upper end of the planet mass spectrum, just below the threshold where objects are usually classified as brown dwarfs (substellar objects that fuse deuterium).  

> **What if there are bigger ones?**  
> Astronomers are constantly discovering new exoplanets, and occasionally a planet larger than HD 100546 b is found. However, as of the latest published data (2024), HD 100546 b remains the largest confirmed planet. If a larger planet is discovered, it would likely be announced in a peer‑reviewed journal and quickly become the new benchmark.

So, in short: **Jupiter** is the largest planet in our Solar System, while **HD 100546 b** is the largest planet that has been observed outside our Solar System to date.
